section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive
text: Jungkyu Kang, 1 Minjae Sung, 1 Jinuk Byun, 1 Oh Joong Kwon, 2,z and Jae Jeong Kim 1,z 1 School of Chemical and Biological Engineering, Institute of Chemical Process, Seoul National University, Gwanak-gu, Seoul 08826, Republic of Korea 2 Department of Energy and Chemical Engineering, Incheon National University, Yeonsu-gu, Incheon 22012, Republic of Korea In this study, superconformal cobalt filling of submicron trenches by electrodeposition is investigated in the presence of 2-mercaptobenzimidazole (MBI), which suppresses both cobalt deposition and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The mechanism through which this single additive enables superconformal cobalt filling is investigated.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0008
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive
text: The mechanism through which this single additive enables superconformal cobalt filling is investigated. The formation and breakdown of the suppression layer are characterized by linear sweep voltammetry and chronoamperometry. The convection-driven local concentration of MBI exerts different suppressing effects on cobalt reduction and the HER, leading to a change in the deposition rate and the current efficiency of cobalt.

text: The convection-driven local concentration of MBI exerts different suppressing effects on cobalt reduction and the HER, leading to a change in the deposition rate and the current efficiency of cobalt. text: When the size of the interconnect reduces below a certain level, resistivity, which is considered as an intrinsic characteristic of the material, increases rapidly because of the resistivity size effect. 1–5 The size effect, which is the origin of the increase in resistivity, is related to the electron mean free path (EMFP). In general, in bulk materials, resistivity is dominated by electron–phonon scattering; therefore, the larger the EMFP, the lower the resistivity.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0012

text: In general, in bulk materials, resistivity is dominated by electron–phonon scattering; therefore, the larger the EMFP, the lower the resistivity. However, as the line width of the interconnect approaches the EMFP, the number of electrons that collide and the grain boundary scattering increases. Therefore, as the line width decreases, resistivity increases rapidly. 5,6 This phenomenon is evidenced at the interconnect line width of <10 nm, which was recently reported; moreover, line resistivity increases to approximately 10 times that of bulk resistivity.

section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive
text: 9,10 The candidate materials that satisfy these conditions are nickel, ruthenium, and cobalt. Among them, cobalt facilitates easy deposition and has a low cost, making it the most appropriate candidate. 10 Extensive studies have been reported on application of cobalt in interconnects. Most of these studies focus on the resistance change and reliability after cobalt deposition through chemical vapor deposition (CVD). 10–18 Conversely, only a few studies on the metallization of cobalt interconnects formed by electrodeposition have been conducted although electrodeposition has various merits.

text: 10–18 Conversely, only a few studies on the metallization of cobalt interconnects formed by electrodeposition have been conducted although electrodeposition has various merits. Electrodeposition has a considerably shorter process time than CVD, and the deposition characteristics can be easily controlled by changing the applied current or voltage and by introducing additives. Additives are widely used to modulate the conditions of plating in electrodeposition.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0017
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive
text: Additives are widely used to modulate the conditions of plating in electrodeposition. In particular, when performing feature filling, additives are essential components that cause a variation in the deposition speed depending on the deposition spots, thereby enabling the performance of superconformal filling. Copper bottom-up filling electrodeposition is performed using a threeadditive system consisting of a suppressor, an accelerator, and a leveler.

Many studies have been conducted on the behavior of additives and their growth mechanisms; however, various additives are still being developed for copper electrodeposition. 19–24 I n the case of nickel, one of the iron group metals, there have also been many studies on additives for superconformal filling.

section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive
text: 19–24 I n the case of nickel, one of the iron group metals, there have also been many studies on additives for superconformal filling. Polyethyleneimine (PEI) and benzimidazole derivatives, such as 2-mercaptobenzimidazole (MBI) and 2-mercapto-5-benzimidazolesulfonic acid (MBIS), were shown to yield void-free feature filling. 25–27 Conversely, for cobalt, there are studies on the additives and mechanisms for cobalt bottom-up filling, although these are still insufficient.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0020
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive
text: 25–27 Conversely, for cobalt, there are studies on the additives and mechanisms for cobalt bottom-up filling, although these are still insufficient. In cobalt bottom-up electrodeposition, some studies explain the mechanism based on the S-shaped negative differential resistance theory 28,29 and the deposition speed difference due to complex formation, 30 which has been suggested in copper bottom-up filling studies. Studies explaining the mechanism based on the interaction with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) involved in cobalt reduction have also been reported.

text: Studies explaining the mechanism based on the interaction with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) involved in cobalt reduction have also been reported. 31,32 As is well known, HER inevitably occurs during cobalt electrodeposition, and one must be familiar with these secondary processes to understand cobalt electrodeposition. These secondary processes increase the pH at the electrode–electrolyte interface, and cobalt hydroxide may precipitate under the increased pH condition.

text: To prevent this, boric acid with a buffering capability is mainly used in Watts-type plating baths. 35,36 Similarly, if an additive that can suppress the HER in the potential region of cobalt deposition is used, the current efficiency can be increased, and the quality of the plating can be improved by inhibiting the increase in pH. In this study, MBI was selected as an additive capable of bottom-up filling by suppressing this additional reaction and increasing the cobalt deposition overpotential.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0072
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive > Conclusions
text: The addition of MBI to a cobalt electrodeposition electrolyte suppressed both the cobalt deposition and the HER. The cobalt suppression effect varied significantly with the MBI concentration, while the HER suppression effect did not. Superconformal filling of submicron trenches was achieved by cobalt electrodeposition with 150 μM of MBI at −1.1 and −1.15 V vs Ag/AgCl. The formation and behavior of the MBI suppression layer were strongly influenced by the potential.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0073
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive > Conclusions
text: The formation and behavior of the MBI suppression layer were strongly influenced by the potential. The MBI suppression layer was formed in approximately 10 s after applying the potential, and it was divided into two cases: one where a partial breakdown occurred, and the other where a relatively strong suppression layer was formed depending on the potential. Cobalt bottom-up filling was possible in the potential region where the partial breakdown occurred.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0074
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive > Conclusions
text: Cobalt bottom-up filling was possible in the potential region where the partial breakdown occurred. In addition, the intensity of the suppression of MBI for cobalt deposition varied according to convection intensity; this is attributable to the concentration difference because of the mass transfer of MBI. At the top where strong convection was maintained, the MBI suppression effect on cobalt deposition was dominant because of the sufficient supply of MBI. However, the convection intensity decreased as it entered the trench, resulting in an MBI concentration gradient.

unit_id: _电化学会志_含析氢反应抑制添加剂的超共形钴电沉积#0075
section: Superconformal Cobalt Electrodeposition with a Hydrogen Evolution Reaction Suppressing Additive > Conclusions
text: However, the convection intensity decreased as it entered the trench, resulting in an MBI concentration gradient. Furthermore, the suppression effect on cobalt deposition was considerably weak at the bottom, while the effect of increasing the current efficiency by suppressing the HER was maintained, enabling the bottom-up filling with a V-shape profile. Through this, we investigated the reason for the occurrence of superconformal cobalt filling, even with the addition of a single additive that exerts only a suppression effect.
